messages:
Maya P: getting paged for steady stream of KV-cache eviction alerts from prod-embeddings pool. seeing retries and a smattering of 5xx from the routing layer. paging now so we can triage. Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: severity=P2, alert=kv_cache_eviction_rate_high, hostgroup=prod-embeddings, triggered at 2026-03-15T14:20Z (thread root)
Eli (SRE): on it. pulled metrics — eviction rate spiked at 14:16, coincides with a burst of long-context requests from a single customer shard. looks like prefix cache thrash.
Aj Chen: can we confirm customer impact? any 429s or downstream timeouts? 
Sri Patel: checking logs — there are ~1200 requests with seq_len>8k in 1m window, many went to dedicated-small pool, some fell back to hosted which introduced extra latency but not full failures. a handful (~12) 5xx.
Maya P: customer-impact: degraded latency for a subset of sessions, not widespread failure. I filed a quick note in the incident doc: https://internal.redwood/incident/1765501234 (draft).
Devops Lead: mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase KV cache size on prod-embeddings hosts (fast but risk OOM), 2) apply alert squelch to non-eviction noisy hosts, 3) rollout a routing override to pin the burst to a larger dedicated pool. prefer 3 for safety.
Eli (SRE): started routing override - redirecting shard x to dedicated-large-02, scaling up by +2 GPUs. command: `infra route --shard shard-x --to dedicated-large-02 --scale 2`
Aj Chen: nice — watching metrics. eviction rate dropping on the impacted hosts, latency normalizing.
Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Action recorded: routing override applied by Eli (SRE).
Maya P: during mitigation we should tune alert thresholds to avoid repeated pages. current alert fires at 10% eviction across pool; we saw short lived bursts. proposal: change to 15% and add a 2min sustained window, and add tag `burst:customer-shard` to alerts so they paginate differently.
Sri Patel: +1 on tag. also suggest adding a secondary metric: kv-cache-miss_ratio > 0.2 for 3m to escalate to P1. that prevents noisy pages for transient evictions.
Aj Chen: who will own the runbook edits? I can update the 'KV cache' runbook with notes and link the routing play. runbook: https://internal.runbooks/kv-cache (needs new section: "burst eviction — routing override")
Maya P: assign Aj and Eli as owners for the new section. Aj to add text, Eli to verify commands. Also add a 'customer impact check' checklist: how many sessions affected, fallback rate, and customer notify threshold.
Eli (SRE): making changes to runbook now. will also add explicit `squelch windows` for known noisy shard patterns and a sample Grafana panel query.
Devops Lead: once runbook PR is ready, we'll create an alert-config change in staging and bake for 24h before prod roll. owners: Aj (PR), Eli (verify), Maya (sign-off).
Maya P: quick note for post-incident: we should add an annotation to the alert rule `recent-burst-mitigation=2026-03-15` and include link to the incident doc. helps correlation for oncall review.
Sri Patel: started a short postmortem draft in the incident doc — root cause: unbounded long-context job from a customer that bypassed batching heuristics; contributing factor: alert threshold tuned for steady-state rather than bursty patterns.
Aj Chen: PR created: https://git.redwood/ops/alerting/pulls/342 (kv-cache threshold + tags + annotation). added testcases and dashboard snapshots.
Incident Bot: :information_source: Incident severity updated to P3 (degraded latency, mitigated).
Maya P: handing off to night oncall at 18:00 UTC — @Eli (SRE) you'll be primary during handoff. please watch the new alert config, and escalate immediately if eviction rate rebounds after routing rollback.
Eli (SRE): acknowledged. will add a pinned note in eng-oncall channel with rollback steps: `infra route --shard shard-x --to default-pool --scale -2` and `infra cache --host <host> --resize  +2G`
Aj Chen: final items: add dashboard panel group "KV cache burst" (latency, eviction_rate, miss_ratio, per-shard top talkers) and a short playbook card linking runbook + rollback commands. I can put that on the console under 'observability' with owner tag = eng-oncall.
Maya P: thanks team. logging post-incident action items: 1) runbook edits (Aj/Eli) 2) alert threshold change staged for 24h (Aj) 3) dashboard + panel (Aj) 4) customer contact if > 100 sessions impacted (Maya) 5) follow-up eval to see if batching heuristics can be tightened (ML infra)
Eli (SRE): leaving a small inline code snippet in runbook for quick triage:

# check top shards by eviction
curl -s "https://metrics.redwood/api/v1/query?query=topk(10, eviction_rate{env=\"prod\"})" | jq .

Maya P: thanks. closing thread once the PR is merged and staging passes. :thumbsup:
